# Current EMA UI Structure Inventory

## Live codebase roots
- `apps/electron/` — desktop shell / preload / runtime bridge / windows state
- `apps/renderer/` — primary frontend/UI app

## Renderer top-level structure
- `src/App.tsx`
- `src/main.tsx`
- `src/components/`
- `src/config/`
- `src/lib/`
- `src/stores/`
- `src/styles/`
- `src/types/`
- `src/vapps/`

## Layout / shell primitives already present
Under `src/components/layout/`:
- `Shell.tsx`
- `Launchpad.tsx`
- `Sidebar.tsx`
- `Dock.tsx`
- `CommandBar.tsx`
- `QuickCapture.tsx`
- `StandaloneAppShell.tsx`
- window chrome / resize / header actions

This suggests the app already has the beginnings of a native shell/launchpad/windowed multi-app model.

## Main structural reality
The renderer currently looks like a **large app garden of many semi-separate vApps/apps**, with a shell/layout layer over them.

## Key interpretation
This is useful because it shows:
- there is already a native UI shell direction
- there is already a vApp/app-window model
- the problem is not lack of surfaces, but lack of reconciliation / conceptual coherence

## Main UI revision question
How should these many app families collapse into a cleaner EMA-native structure?
Likely candidates:
- Shell / HQ
- Workstreams / Agent Work
- Knowledge Graph / Canon / Recall
- Code Region
- Host Ops / Runtime Reality
- Chronicle / Review / Gaps
- Capture / Inbox / Daily Steering
